definitions.explanation: A situation where two propositions or principles, each appearing valid in itself, are mutually contradictory; an irreconcilable conflict between two equally reasonable positions.

examples.japanese: ⟦{仕事|しごと}→仕事：00480_shigoto⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{家庭|かてい}→家庭：12315_katei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{二律背反|にりつはいはん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{悩|なや}んでいる→悩む：02380_nayamu⟧。
examples.english: I'm struggling with the conflict between work and family.

examples.japanese: ⟦{自由|じゆう}→自由：01148_jiyuu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{平等|びょうどう}→平等：03590_byoudou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{二律背反|にりつはいはん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{哲学|てつがく}→哲学：03548_tetsugaku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{重要|じゅうよう}→重要：01575_juuyou⟧⟦な→な：09497_na⟧⟦テーマ→テーマ：17684_teema⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: The antinomy between freedom and equality is an important topic in philosophy.

examples.japanese: ⟦{経済|けいざい}→経済：01394_keizai⟧⟦{成長|せいちょう}→成長：03290_seichou⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{環境|かんきょう}→環境：00174_kankyou⟧⟦{保護|ほご}→保護：03625_hogo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{二律背反|にりつはいはん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{関係|かんけい}→関係：01298_kankei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われる→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: Economic growth and environmental protection are said to be in an antinomical relationship.

notes:
ORIGIN: This is a Japanese translation of the philosophical term "antinomy" (from Greek). It was notably used by the German philosopher Immanuel Kant to describe contradictions in pure reason.

STRUCTURE: {二|に} (two) + {律|りつ} (laws/principles) + {背|はい} (against) + {反|はん} (oppose). Literally: two laws opposing each other.

USAGE: Used in philosophical, academic, and general contexts to describe situations where two principles or goals conflict with each other.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{二律背反|にりつはいはん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{関係|かんけい}→関係：01298_kankei⟧ (an antinomical relationship)
・{二律背反|にりつはいはん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{陥|おちい}る→陥る：14537_ochiiru⟧ (to fall into a contradiction)

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
・⟦{矛盾|むじゅん}→矛盾：05215_mujun⟧ (contradiction)
・⟦ジレンマ→ジレンマ：29389_jirenma⟧ (dilemma)
・⟦{板挟|いたばさ}み→板挟み：07723_itabasami⟧ (caught between two conflicting forces)
